Robot models from Denavit-Hartenberg parameters

Source: R/dh-model.R
robot_dh.Rd

Builds a serial robot_model whose link frames coincide with the DH frames. Link i is named "link<i>" and its frame is DH frame i; the root is "base" (DH frame 0). For revolute joints theta is the joint offset and \(q_i\) is added to it; for prismatic joints d is the offset and \(q_i\) is added to it. Standard and modified conventions are never mixed in one model; see dh_transform() for the formulas.

robot_dh(
  a,
  alpha,
  d,
  theta,
  joint_type = "revolute",
  convention = c("standard", "modified"),
  limits = NULL,
  base = robot_pose(),
  tool = NULL,
  mass = NULL,
  com = NULL,
  inertia = NULL,
  name = "dh_robot"
)

Arguments

a, alpha, d, theta

Numeric vectors of equal length with one entry per link.

joint_type

Character vector of "revolute" or "prismatic".

convention

"standard" or "modified".

limits

Optional matrix with one row c(lower, upper) per joint.

base

Optional base pose.

tool

Optional pose of a "tool" frame in the last link frame.

mass, com, inertia

Optional inertial parameters.

name

Model name.

Value

A robot_model with extra field dh holding the parameters.

Details

Optional inertial parameters are given per link in the DH link frame: mass is a vector, com a matrix with one row per link, and inertia a list of 3 by 3 matrices about the center of mass.

Examples

robot <- robot_dh(a = c(1, 1), alpha = c(0, 0), d = c(0, 0),
                  theta = c(0, 0), joint_type = c("revolute", "revolute"))
pose_translation(robot_fk(robot, c(pi / 2, pi / 2)))
#> [1] -1  1  0
